title: Serre's quasi-compact vanishing criterion
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Assume that $X$ is quasi-compact and that $H^1(X,\mathcal I)=0$ for every quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ [pqf-def-coherent, pqf-def-cohomology]. Then $X$ is affine.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma Tag 01XF (label lemma-quasi-compact-h1-zero-covering), lines 283-388

proof.text: For each closed point, apply the split closed-point lifting lemma to obtain a section whose affine basic open contains that point. Let W be the union of all affine basic opens. The complement is closed; compactness and the T₀ property imply that a nonempty complement contains a closed point, contradiction. Compactness extracts a finite subcover.
For the resulting finite set s of sections, apply the split finite-basic-cover cohomological lemma to obtain Ideal.span s = ⊤.
Apply the affine basic-open unit-ideal criterion to the finite family and its affine basic opens to conclude IsAffine X.
